requirement: Clip gradients before an optimizer step so their combined L2 norm never exceeds a limit, skipping parameters without gradients and refusing to continue on inf or NaN.
skeleton: An EPS constant and clip_grad_norm validating max_norm, gathering non-None gradients, computing the global L2 norm, handling non-finite norms, and scaling in place only when above the limit.
caption: Global gradient clipping in the style of torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_, written with the standard library math module against duck-typed parameters whose grad is a list of floats or None, with no third-party imports. clip_grad_norm(params, max_norm, *, error_if_nonfinite=True) raises ValueError unless max_norm is positive and collects the gradients of parameters whose grad is not None. It computes the joint L2 norm over every element; a non-finite norm raises RuntimeError when error_if_nonfinite is set and is otherwise returned untouched. The coefficient is max_norm over the norm plus EPS, and only when it is below one every gradient list is scaled in place with slice assignment. It returns the norm before clipping. The fixture asserts joint scaling, untouched small gradients, in-place modification, skipped None gradients, raising and reporting non-finite norms, and max_norm validation.

constraints: max_norm must be positive, else ValueError
Parameters whose grad is None are skipped
The norm is the L2 norm over all gradients together
A non-finite norm raises RuntimeError unless error_if_nonfinite is False
Gradients are only scaled down, in place

rationale.teaches: Compute one global L2 norm, scale by max_norm over norm plus eps only when that is below one, mutate the gradient buffers in place, and fail loudly on non-finite norms.
rationale.why: Rebinding instead of mutating leaves the real gradients unclipped, always scaling inflates small gradients, and ignoring inf silently poisons every weight on the next step.

ops.docstring: Global gradient norm clipping in the style of torch's clip_grad_norm_.

candidates.why_wrong: Frozen parameters with a None grad crash the clipping with TypeError.
Small gradients are scaled up to max_norm instead of left alone.
The scaled list is rebound locally, so the real gradients never change.
The L1 sum is used instead of the L2 norm, clipping far too hard.
Infinite gradients are returned silently instead of raising RuntimeError.
